title: Change a click pen's refill: spring into the nose, new refill in through it, clicker back in with its hook to the clip
instruction: Put the new refill in the pen: the spring into the barrel's nose, the refill in point-first through it, then push the clicker in until it latches, its hook toward the clip.
context: Changing a pen's refill is a familiar desk job. On a one-piece click pen such as the Clip Click, the clicker comes out of the barrel's back end and the refill and its loose spring come out after it. Putting it back takes care: the spring has to go down into the nose first, the new refill point-first through it, and the clicker in with its hook toward the clip, or it doesn't latch. A pen put together without its spring looks finished but doesn't click.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. A grey desk pen stand, fixed: a 3 x 16 cm base, 4 mm thick, centred at (25, -2), with three tubes in a row along y, 6 cm apart: a 7.6 mm bore 2 cm tall at (25, 4), an 8.3 mm bore 4 cm tall at (25, -2) and a 5.2 mm bore 3 cm tall at (25, -8). The pen is a Clip Click-type click ballpoint, taken apart. In the 8.3 mm hole stands its clear one-piece barrel nose-down (12.7 cm long, 8 mm across, widening to 10 mm over its back 5 cm, a 1.5 cm nose cone, 6.5 mm bore), its pocket clip on the robot's left (+y). In the 7.6 mm hole stands its blue clicker button-up (5 cm long, about 6 mm across, a 5 mm button cap, its latch hook on the +y side). In the 5.2 mm hole stands the new refill point-down (10.3 cm long, trimmed from 10.7 cm, 3 mm plastic ink tube, brass point 6 mm long and 2 mm across, a spring stop 2.2 cm from the point). The pen's steel spring (3 cm long) stands on end at (20, -14). Both arms start at the ready pose with open grippers. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Spring back in place: its centre within 3.25 mm of the barrel's axis and within 5 cm of the nose tip, or round the refill's front. Refill in: its point within 1.5 mm of the barrel's axis, 8 to 30 mm from the nose tip, in line within 6 deg, the spring round its front (centre within 1.2 mm of the refill's axis, against its stop). Clicker latched: its button 6 to 10 mm out of the barrel, its lower end within 1.5 mm of the axis, in line within 6 deg, its hook within 20 deg of the clip's side. 1.0 (success): all three, both hands' tool points 4 cm from every part and no part moving over 1 cm/s, held for 1 s (the score reads 1.0 as soon as this holds; the trial ends with success once it has held 1 s). Otherwise, at the end: 0.75 all three; 0.5 spring in and refill in; 0.25 spring in only; 0 if the spring is not in place, whatever else is done. Real trial: the barrel is clear, so the spring in the nose and the refill through it can be seen; measure the button's height (ruler) and check the hook is under the clip, then click it: the point comes out and goes back only with the spring in.
reset_notes: Nothing is used up: pull the clicker out, tip the refill and spring out of the barrel, and stand the barrel, clicker and refill back in their holes and the spring on its mark.
fidelity: Rigid bodies of convex pieces, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Sizes measured from a pen of this design. The spring is a rigid 5.2 mm tube with funnelled ends (real 4 mm, springy); the refill's stop is a 5 mm collar and its end is rounded. The barrel is held fixed by the stand; its bore is 6.5 mm throughout. The clicker is 0.35 mm loose in the bore and its latch is left out: its turning is damped instead, and latched means 8 mm out with the hook to the clip.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps; the right arm went to the stand and moved among the parts, but the spring never went into the barrel); demo: 1.0 (1,582 steps, same in a repeat run). Steps 1-2 only (no clicker): 0.5; without the spring: 0.
